versions.changelog:
- Updated installation instructions in documentation to recommend pip as the primary method.
- Clarified alternative installation options for Linux/macOS and Windows.
- Improved the `aitun` CLI installation reference for consistency.
- Removed legacy documentation file: skill-card.md.

- Added pip-based install option for aitun (cross-platform support in SKILL.md).
- Updated metadata to include both pip and uv installation methods.
- Removed skill-card.md from the repository.

- Added Windows PowerShell installation instructions.
- No other user-facing changes.

- Added explicit version number (4.0.2) to SKILL.md.
- Updated installation instructions to use the official shell script (`curl -fsSL https://aitun.cc/install.sh | bash`) instead of `pip install aitun`.
- Clarified that the `-p` (port) flag is optional and explained TCP-only usage with `--tcp-ports`.
- Improved CLI documentation to cover both HTTP and TCP-only forwarding scenarios.
- Removed legacy metadata and skill description files (_meta.json, skill-card.md) for simplification.

- Added version field to SKILL.md and updated usage documentation.
- Updated installation instructions to recommend install.sh script instead of pip.
- Clarified CLI reference: `-p` flag is now optional—omit it for TCP-only mode using `--tcp-ports`.
- Noted that the local service must be running before starting aitun when `-p` is used.
- Removed unused files: _meta.json and skill-card.md.

- Added version field to SKILL.md.
- Clarified that the -p flag is optional and can be omitted for TCP-only mode with --tcp-ports.
- Updated CLI reference to reflect new flag usage and TCP-only support.
- Noted that the local service must be running before starting aitun when using the -p flag.
- Removed _meta.json and skill-card.md files.
Remove API Reference, Common Mistakes sections and -s SERVER flag from CLI Reference

Major update: Fixed incorrect CLI flags (-l, --free, --subdomain, aitun-connect removed). Added CLI Reference table and Common Mistakes section. Free tunnel now uses path-based URL (aitun.cc/abc123). Corrected subdomain registration API to include domain_base.
Removed AiTun Connect tool, simplified free tunnel flow with auto client_id persistence, updated API docs
Initial release - expose local web pages to the public internet via secure tunnels
